elements.label: Figure 4.9
elements.description: Line chart with two series, Ethnic minority (teal) and Kinh (orange). Y-axis: "Share of cohort population (%)", scale 0 to 120 in steps of 20. X-axis: single-year ages 10 to 25. Values are not printed, so approximate readings: Ethnic minority: 10 ~100, 11 ~92, 12 ~89, 13 ~92, 14 ~85, 15 ~70, 16 ~55, 17 ~40, 18 ~28, 19 ~14, 20 ~15, 21 ~6, 22 ~7, 23 ~9, 24 ~0, 25 ~1. Kinh: 10 ~100, 11 ~100, 12 ~99, 13 ~95, 14 ~94, 15 ~88, 16 ~83, 17 ~82, 18 ~70, 19 ~56, 20 ~53, 21 ~43, 22 ~31, 23 ~14, 24 ~6, 25 ~1. Source: World Bank staff calculation using VHLSS2020. The Kinh curve stays above the ethnic minority curve at every age, and both decline from about age 14-15, with the ethnic minority decline steeper and reaching near zero earlier.

elements.label: Figure 4.10
elements.description: Grouped bar chart with Y-axis "Share of households (%)", scale 0 to 100 in steps of 20. X-axis categories: Improved water and Improved sanitation. Series: Ethnic minority (teal) and Kinh (orange). Values are not printed, so approximate readings: Improved water: Ethnic minority ~75, Kinh ~95. Improved sanitation: Ethnic minority ~52, Kinh ~88. Source: MICS Survey (UNICEF, 2014). Kinh households are higher than ethnic minority households on both indicators, with the largest gap for sanitation.
